09:00.headline: Myth: JUCO is a last resort
09:00.topic: Myth-buster: junior college as an intentional pathway (innings, development, transfer to four-year, cost)

graphic.headline: Myth: *JUCO is a last resort*
graphic.sub: For many players, junior college is a smart route: real innings, time to develop, and a path to four-year programs.

captions.instagram:
Myth: JUCO is where players end up when nothing else works out.

Reality: for a lot of baseball families, junior college is a smart, intentional choice.

⚾ He can compete for real innings early instead of waiting his turn.
⚾ He gets time to get stronger, faster and more polished.
⚾ Many JUCO players move on to four-year programs after one or two seasons.
⚾ Costs are often lower than at a four-year school.

Best fit beats biggest name. The right first stop is the one where he plays and keeps growing.

Monday Myth-Buster: "JUCO is a last resort."

We hear this from parents all the time, and it sells junior college short.

For many players, JUCO is a deliberate first step:
✅ A real chance to compete for innings as a freshman
✅ A year or two to add strength, speed and polish before the next move
✅ A well-worn path to four-year programs, with coaches who recruit JUCO players
✅ Often a lower cost than starting at a four-year school

It isn't the right path for every player, and that's the point. The goal is finding where he'll actually play and develop, not chasing the biggest name on the list.

13:00.headline: D2 vs. D3: what's different?
13:00.topic: Know your level: D2 partial athletic aid + Eligibility Center vs D3 no athletic aid; grades matter at both

captions.instagram:
D2 or D3? They're both great college baseball. They just work differently.

⚾ D2 programs can offer athletic scholarships, usually split into partial awards.
⚾ D3 programs don't offer athletic scholarships. Aid comes from academic merit and need-based packages.
⚾ To play D2, he needs to be certified through the NCAA Eligibility Center. D3 doesn't require that certification.
⚾ At both levels, strong grades widen his options.

Neither level is "better." The right fit depends on his numbers, his grades and what your family needs.

Know your level: what's actually different between D2 and D3 baseball?

A lot of families lump them together. Here's the practical difference for parents:

⚾ Money: D2 programs can offer athletic scholarships, usually as partial awards. D3 programs don't offer athletic scholarships, so aid comes through academic merit and need-based packages.
⚾ Paperwork: D2 requires certification through the NCAA Eligibility Center. D3 doesn't require that certification, but admissions standards still matter.
⚾ Grades: at both levels, a strong GPA opens more doors and can make a big difference in the final cost.

Both levels have competitive baseball and real development. The better question is which one fits your player's numbers, academics and budget.
